IV. INFORMATION TO DEMONSTRATE THAT ALL POSSIBLE PLANNING TO MINIMIZE HARM IS OR WILL BE INCLUDED IN THE HIGHWAY PROPOSAL 
A. The Agency Responsible for Furnishing the Highway Right-Of-Way
No land will be taken or is necessary on a permanent basis from the Cook County Forest Preserve District for right-of-way in order to implement this improvement.
A small amount of land 0.17 acres will be required from the Forest Preserve District as a temporary construction easement for the removal of bridge wing walls over Thorn Creek and to provide a safer grade for the entrance driveway into the Forest Preserve District site.
B. Provisions for Compensating or Replacing the Section 4(f) Land and Improvements Thereon, Including the Status of any Agreements.
The impact of the Section 4(f) Land as a result of this proposed improvement should be minimal.
In a Letter from the Cook County Forest Preserve District Dated September 4, 1974, the District Stated:
"It is our opinion that the temporary use will not have any significant effect on the recreational opportunities of the community."
Evidence of coordination and concurrence by the local jurisdiction during the various phases of this project are contained in Appendix "A". This includes coordination and comments received from the U.S. Department of Interior, U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, Forest Preserve District of Cook County, and U.S. Department of Agriculture, with an evaluation and disposition of these comments contained in Appendix "C".
